subject: general
question: Mica is which type of mineral?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Non-metallic**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Mica is a type of mineral that falls under the category of **non-metallic minerals**.
 
• It is known for its **excellent cleavage properties**, allowing it to be split into thin, flexible sheets.
 
• Mica is primarily used in the **electronics and electrical industries** due to its insulating properties and resistance to heat.
 
• It is also utilized in the production of **cosmetics, paints, and plastics** for its reflective and refractive properties.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Non-metallic minerals**

 
 
• These minerals do not contain metals and are typically used in industries based on their physical and chemical properties rather than their metallic content.
 
• Examples include mica, limestone, gypsum, and quartz.
 
 
 
• **Properties of Mica**
 
 
• Mica is highly resistant to electricity, making it an excellent electrical insulator.
 
• It can withstand high temperatures, which is why it is used in thermal insulation materials.
 
 
 
• **Uses of Mica**
 
 
• In the electronics industry, mica is used in capacitors and insulators.
 
• In the cosmetic industry, it is used to add shimmer to products like eyeshadows and highlighters.
 
• In the construction industry, it is used as an additive in paint to improve brightness and durability.
 
 
 
• **Extraction and Processing**
 
 
• Mica is mined from pegmatite deposits, which are often found in igneous rocks.
 
• After extraction, it is processed and graded based on its size, quality, and intended use.
